live_frontier_title: Paper-I beta extraction / marginal-defect orthogonality and UV-defect amplitude audit
current_determination: R64 separates source-attested coordinate triangularity from the stronger dynamical projection triangularity hypothesized in R63. CMP119 Eq. (2.24) prescribes the localized coupling sequence from g_{j-1}, beta_j(g_{j-1}) and phi_j with no explicit E/R/B argument, while Eq. (2.25) places the regular contribution in the complementary coordinate after subtracting beta_j(g_{j-1}) A(phi_j,U_k). Thus DeclaredCoordinateTriangularity and MarginalSubtractionArchitecture are source-attested. This does not yet prove the Banach-map identity D_K T_x=0 for arbitrary nearby complete densities, nor exact zero-marginal projection of the residual activity; the Paper-I definition of beta_j must be recovered. Cross-cutoff use also requires CrossDepthMarginalTailCoherence because beta_j, phi_j and Lambda_j are scale-indexed. If canonical generated trajectories with a common coupling tail are coherent under reindexing, the R62 comparison can set delta x=0 and reduce loss of memory to the complementary sector without a full stable graph. Published absolute activity bounds do not yet give a two-trajectory derivative contraction. A second possible closure route is now visible: because the extra layer occurs at g_UV^(N)->0 and several complementary sectors carry positive powers of g, the one-layer compatibility defect may itself vanish summably, but the Paper-I E-sector bound (I.1.18) remains unextracted.
major_new_results: CMP119 Eq. (2.24) source-attests triangularity of the declared running-coupling coordinate with respect to the named E/R/B coordinates.
CMP119 Eq. (2.25) source-attests the marginal-subtraction architecture: beta_j A(phi_j,U) is removed from each regular scale contribution.
Declared-coordinate triangularity is distinguished from general projection triangularity D_K T_x=0; only the former is presently source-attested.
The full R63 stable graph is no longer the default theorem target if canonical cross-cutoff trajectories share a coherent prescribed coupling tail.
CrossDepthMarginalTailCoherence is isolated as a separate indexed source obligation involving beta_j, phi_j and the regular-domain sequence.
Complementary-coordinate dependence on g is source-visible, so only one-way triangularity is expected.
A second endpoint-Cauchy route is identified: summably small UV one-layer defects plus bounded propagation may replace uniform strict complementary contraction.
negative_results: Do not infer D_K T_x=0 merely from the displayed scalar form of Eq. (2.24).
Do not infer exact zero marginal projection of the residual regular activity from Eq. (2.25) before recovering the Paper-I beta extraction definition.
Do not infer cross-depth tail nesting from a scale-indexed within-trajectory recursion without a reindexing/coherence theorem.
Do not infer two-trajectory contraction from absolute CMP116/CMP119/CMP122 activity bounds.
Do not use the R-sector g^kappa0 bound as a bound on the entire one-layer defect before extracting the E-sector bound.
Do not infer continuum construction or a mass gap from coordinate triangularity or UV-defect smallness.
